exposure: adequacy of weight for gestational age at birth (Small for Gestational Age vs. Adequate for Gestational Age)
type of intrauterine growth (symmetric vs. asymmetric for SGA)
outcome: neurobehavioral development (evaluated using the Neurobehavioral Assessment of the Preterm Infant - NAPI)
cohort: 55 preterm infants hospitalized in a neonatal intermediate care unit.
finding: No significant differences were observed in neurobehavioral development (NAPI domains) between preterm infants born small for gestational age (SGA) and those adequate for gestational age (AGA), nor within SGA subgroups based on symmetric or asymmetric intrauterine growth.
cross-section timing: At a postconceptional age between 32 weeks and 36 weeks and 6 days.
birth_weight: Categorized as Small for Gestational Age (SGA) or Adequate for Gestational Age (AGA).
gest_age: Mean gestational age at birth was 32.0 weeks; evaluations were performed at a postconceptional age between 32 and 36 weeks and 6 days.
